title: Color Order · Teams
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Color Order · Teams with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Arrange three colored papers in a row and cover them after a brief look. The lead names the colors in order. The colors are named in their original order. Form two teams. Each team has four turns; only the lead’s teammates respond or assist. Each success earns the team one point. The higher team score wins; ties are shared.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4–8 players; materials: Three different colored papers and a cloth.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Color Order, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The colors are named in their original order.
recall.why: The colors are named in their original order.

game.materials: Three different colored papers and a cloth
